standard.title: Manipulate elements to communicate ideas
standard.description: manipulate elements of music to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning when composing and practising for performance
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can select and combine elements of music when composing (AC9AMU2C01) and have practised documentation using signs, symbols and recordings. They can combine two elements for expressive effect and justify their selections. They have not yet manipulated elements strategically to communicate specific ideas, perspectives or meaning across a sustained composition.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students manipulate elements of music to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning when composing and practising for performance, using notation, documentation or recording to capture their work.

nodes.label: Manipulating vs selecting elements
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students understand that manipulating elements means actively changing, shaping and controlling them throughout a composition — not just choosing them at the start.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate one manipulation of a musical element during a composition (e.g. making a section get louder over time, or changing a melody's rhythm) and explain what effect the manipulation creates.
nodes.typical_width: Manipulate elements dynamically within compositions — varying dynamics across sections, extending or shortening rhythmic values, changing tempo for dramatic effect, altering articulation; describe how each manipulation shapes the music's meaning or mood.
wider: Compose a section where one element (e.g. dynamics) gradually changes across the whole section — describe what that arc communicates
Take a known song and deliberately manipulate two elements (e.g. tempo and articulation) to create a completely different mood — compare before and after
nodes.hinge_reason: The conceptual leap from 'selecting elements' (Y1-2) to 'manipulating elements' is the core of this standard. Students who remain at selection level — choosing elements but not actively shaping them throughout — cannot meet the descriptor's command term and cannot access AC9AMU6C01 which requires manipulating elements plus compositional devices.

response_modes.reason: Make the distinction explicit: 'Selecting means choosing which elements to use. Manipulating means changing how an element behaves during the music — making it grow, shrink, shift, transform.' Use guided analysis of recordings to identify manipulations before students attempt them in their own compositions.

success_criteria: Demonstrates at least one active manipulation of an element within a composition (not just its initial selection)
Can describe the effect of the manipulation on the music's mood or meaning

nodes.label: Communicating ideas through manipulation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can manipulate elements of music specifically to communicate an idea, perspective or meaning — e.g. expressing dramatic action, emotion or character.
nodes.minimum_width: Compose a short piece where element manipulations serve a specific communicative intention (e.g. tension building, a character emerging, a story unfolding).
nodes.typical_width: Manipulate elements to express different characters or dramatic action in compositions for screen-based works or drama; write lyrics for songs that communicate ideas; combine composed and improvised sections that serve different communicative purposes (e.g. composed theme + improvised soundscape); work in pairs or groups on ostinatos or accompaniments that support a larger musical idea.
wider: Compose music to accompany a re-telling of a familiar story — map which manipulations correspond to which story events, and explain each choice
Learn and compose music associated with a specific cultural style — identify which element manipulations are characteristic of that style
nodes.hinge_reason: Connecting element manipulation to communicative intent — rather than to aesthetic preference — is the critical move this standard makes. Without it, students compose music they like but cannot explain or justify in terms of ideas or meaning. AC9AMU6C01 explicitly requires communicating 'ideas, perspectives and/or meaning'; if this connection is not established at Y3-4, that requirement becomes inaccessible.

response_modes.reason: Communicative purpose becomes clearer with more compositional contexts. Composing for drama, screen, songs and accompaniments each require different types of communicative manipulation — each context adds a new angle on how elements serve meaning.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of communicative purposes available at Y3-4 (storytelling, character expression, cultural identity, cross-curricular themes) is genuinely rich — each purpose requires different element manipulations and develops different compositional thinking.
success_criteria: Composes a piece with a stated communicative intention
Can identify which element manipulations serve that intention and explain how they do so

nodes.label: Notation and documentation for practice
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use notation or documentation to capture their compositions and use this during rehearsal to practise and refine the work.
nodes.minimum_width: Document a composition using at least one notation format (graphic, lead-sheet, staff, audio) and use the documentation during at least one rehearsal.
nodes.typical_width: Use multiple documentation formats depending on the composition type — lead-sheets for songs with lyrics, graphic notation for soundscapes, audio recordings for improvisations; use documentation to practise independently and in groups; revise documentation when the composition changes.
wider: Use a story-boarding app or digital template to document where music will be used in a media work — connect notation to the visual timeline
Compare two different notation formats for the same piece (e.g. a graphic score and a lead-sheet) — discuss which is more useful for rehearsal and why

response_modes.reason: Students who only know one notation format default to it regardless of whether it suits the composition type. Building a repertoire of documentation formats (graphic, lead-sheet, audio recording, staff notation) gives students appropriate tools for different musical contexts.

success_criteria: Documents a composition in at least one notation format with enough accuracy to use in rehearsal
Uses the documentation during rehearsal to maintain or refine the composition
